# User instructions

## Git workflow

Start every new feature on a fresh branch cut from up-to-date `master`/`main`:

1. Fetch and fast-forward the default branch (`git fetch origin && git pull --ff-only`).
2. Create the feature branch from it (`git checkout -b <topic>`).
3. Only then begin work.

Do not start feature work on a stale default branch or directly on `master`/`main`.

## Answer verification

For any question about whether a third-party tool supports a feature

# User instructions

## Git workflow

Start every new feature on a fresh branch cut from up-to-date `master`/`main`:

1. Fetch and fast-forward the default branch (`git fetch origin && git pull --ff-only`).
2. Create the feature branch from it (`git checkout -b <topic>`).
3. Only then begin work.

Do not start feature work on a stale default branch or directly on `master`/`main`.

## Answer verification

For any question about whether a third-party tool supports a feature

## Git workflow

Start every new feature on a fresh branch cut from up-to-date `master`/`main`:

1. Fetch and fast-forward the default branch (`git fetch origin && git pull --ff-only`).
2. Create the feature branch from it (`git checkout -b <topic>`).

# User instructions

## Git workflow

Start every new feature on a fresh branch cut from up-to-date `master`/`main`:

2. Create the feature branch from it (`git checkout -b <topic>`).
